indian.headline: Markets fell on RBI's first rate hike in years, but new IPO listings surged.
indian.lead: Markets fell on RBI's first rate hike in years, but new IPO listings surged.
indian.brief: Sensex dropped 0.59% and Nifty 50 fell 0.76% after the Reserve Bank raised its key lending rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, its first increase since 2023.
why: RBI raised its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% to combat inflation risks, triggering broad selling pressure across rate-sensitive sectors like IT and banking.

New company listings outperformed the broader market: SRIT India surged 19%, Kanohar Electricals jumped 15%, and Vans Electroengineerings debuted at 90% premium, showing investor confidence in fresh IPOs despite the selloff.

Jewellery and consumer stocks bucked the trend—Deepa Jewellers rallied 13% on strong Q1 results and Kalyan Jewellers gained 2% on 26% revenue growth, as sector-specific strength offset index weakness.
indian.narrative:
India's stock market closed lower on October 7 as the Reserve Bank of India raised its benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, marking its first rate hike since 2023. The move spooked investors concerned about costlier borrowing ahead. The Sensex fell 0.59% and Nifty 50 dropped 0.76%, while Bank Nifty eased just 0.13%. IT stocks bore the brunt, sliding 1.3%, followed by pharma's 0.4% loss and banking's modest 0.1% decline.

Yet beneath the headline weakness, a divergent market emerged. Newly listed companies and select sectors defied gravity. SRIT India surged 19% on its debut, Kanohar Electricals jumped 15% after doubling profits, and Vans Electroengineerings listed at a 90% premium. Jewellery stocks also held firm—Deepa Jewellers rallied 13% on robust Q1 growth, and Kalyan Jewellers gained 2% on 26% revenue growth. These pockets of strength suggest investors are selectively buying quality earnings and growth stories, even as they trim exposure to rate-sensitive sectors in the face of tighter monetary policy ahead.

us.headline: US stocks closed higher across the board, led by semiconductor strength and AI-driven growth optimism.
us.lead: US stocks closed higher across the board, led by semiconductor strength and AI-driven growth optimism.
us.brief: S&P 500 gained 0.58%, Nasdaq rose 0.45%, and Dow climbed 0.49% as tech and energy sectors outperformed.
why: Marvell Technology beat profit forecasts and signaled strong future growth, boosting chipmakers and the broader tech sector by 0.5%.
Google's nuclear power deal signals massive AI infrastructure investment, reinforcing belief that big tech companies will sustain high spending and growth.
Falling US bond yields eased rate-hike worries, making stocks more attractive than safe assets like bonds or gold.
S&P 500 reaching all-time highs on 'Magnificent Seven' momentum encouraged buying across the market despite some caution in healthcare.
us.narrative:
US stock markets ended October 7 in the green, with all three major indices posting modest but solid gains. The S&P 500's fresh record-breaking performance was anchored by a resurgence in the 'Magnificent Seven'—the seven largest US tech firms—after a year of underperformance. Semiconductor company Marvell's earnings beat and bullish guidance energized the chip sector, while Google's announced nuclear power purchase from Constellation Energy highlighted the immense electricity needs driving AI investment across Silicon Valley.

Underlying the rally was a drop in US bond yields, which reduced expectations for near-term interest rate hikes and made stocks comparatively more attractive. Energy stocks also held steady at +0.5%, while financials gained 0.2%. Healthcare was the sole laggard, slipping 0.2%, possibly due to profit-taking or sector rotation. Gold remained unmoved around $4,165 per ounce, reflecting the calmer rate-hike outlook. However, global observers noted caution: the World Bank and IMF both warned that AI-driven growth, while powerful, risks concentrating wealth and opportunity among rich nations.
